history.summary: 16th-century Vijayanagara Shiva temple standing inside Vellore Fort, surrounded by the fort moat. The name means 'Shiva residing in water', from the perennial natural spring beneath the main lingam. Renowned for its Kalyana Mandapam with monolithic granite pillars carved with rearing yalis, warrior horsemen and rotating stone rings cut from single blocks. Worship was suspended for nearly 400 years under foreign control of the fort; devotees peacefully brought the deity back and restored regular worship in 1981. The temple now functions under government administration (HR&CE) with the ASI-preserved fort complex. The Ganga Gouri Theertham well is the temple's holy spring, and the site is locally equated with Kashi (Shiva, Ganga theertha and Bhairava all present). NOTE: coordinates are the Vellore Fort centre; the geocoder does not resolve the temple itself - the temple stands inside the fort walls.

name: Jalakandeswarar Temple
town_description: Vellore is a major city in northern Tamil Nadu and the headquarters of Vellore district; the Jalakandeswarar temple stands in the heart of the city inside the 16th-century Vellore Fort, whose moated ramparts also hosted the 1806 Sepoy Mutiny.

travel.road: Vellore Fort is central Vellore; Vellore is ~138 km from Chennai by road/rail on the Chennai-Bengaluru corridor

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Chitra Pournami (Apr-May) is the main 10-day festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:30 AM - 1:00 PM and 5:00 PM - 8:30 PM daily; entry free
